📍San Mateo, CA

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give leadership a live aerial view over long distances during emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection.

Why: Skydio says a single MegaDock, with F10's 30-mile flight radius, can put nearly 3,000 square miles within reach of one launch location.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Concept per Skydio. Deploying to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is its first fixed-wing aircraft. The company also introduced Controller 2, rolling out internationally this fall, and two software platforms, Asset Command and Security Command, which are available to purchase now with general availability early next year. Skydio also said the new Transparency Dashboard arrives later this year.

fields.headline: STATE PICKS PARAVISION FOR DIGITAL ID WORK
fields.deck: A five-year firm-fixed-price contract could reach $6.5 million, with $1.3 million obligated first.

stories.caption:
The State Department has awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $6.5 million, tied to what federal procurement records call "digital detection/identity assurance." The contract was signed September 23, with $1.3 million committed at the outset and performance possible through September 22, 2031.

The department ran the competition under simplified acquisition procedures as a small-business set-aside and received one offer. Public award records do not name the Paravision products bought. The description overlaps with Paravision's deepfake detection work, which flags manipulated and AI-generated faces, but the record does not confirm whether the award covers deepfake detection, liveness detection, facial recognition or other software.

This is a much larger deal than an earlier State Department purchase from the company. On April 30, the department bought a separate $24,717 software license through a purchase card. Public records do not say what that software was or whether it served as a test or pilot for the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, 17OCT26

Image: Paravision (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH / SEASATS

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, in the Gulf of America.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and the area one asset can cover at a time.

Private company → Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures.

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed in the Gulf of America, expanding operations that have run on the Rio Grande since January 2026, per Seasats.

Seasats said on Oct. 2, 2026 that it has deployed a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels for U.S. maritime border security work. The boats launched from the Texas coast and will patrol the Gulf without anyone aboard, building on the company's earlier work on the Rio Grande this year.

Each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. Its solar power supports multi-month time on station, and two people can launch and recover one without heavy equipment. Sensor payloads have included infrared and electro-optical cameras, signals gear and sonar.

Seasats says a fleet of these boats can keep watch over an area that crewed vessels only see in snapshots. Company CEO Mike Flanigan has said the vessels can stay out in conditions where a crew would not be sent. The company also reports more than $100 million in U.S. government contracts.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

Image: prnewswire.com (courtesy)

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE TOOLS IN AFRICA
fields.deck: The first accelerated capability event is set for spring 2027 in Morocco.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to trial new systems in Africa, with the aim of getting them into Soldiers' hands within 180 days.

The command's first accelerated capability event, known as an ACE, is planned for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. Its focus is counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, aimed at shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner, following Soldier-led demonstrations in February and March 2027 and an operational assessment in April and May.

The Army says Africa's open spectrum, uncongested airspace and varied terrain let Soldiers validate solutions in theater and scale them across the service. G-TEAD assigned a team to SETAF-AF in summer 2026 to link operational needs with rapid acquisition resources.

Source: U.S. Army, Oct. 16, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Caitlinn Belcher

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

media.credit: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Caitlinn Belcher

fields.headline: TOP DEFENSE DEVELOPMENTS
fields.story_02: Lockheed unveils PAC-3 Edge for Army

stories.caption:
Here are three MilCityUSA stories from the past week, each linked to its original card.

Microchip Technology has acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology to Microchip's space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin has unveiled PAC-3 Edge as its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3 at Camp Blanding, Sept. 26 to Oct. 2, testing how Tactical Assault Kit location data, unmanned-system information and video feeds can share one operational picture. The Guard also noted that dedicated technical specialists were critical to keeping that picture working.

Source: MilCityUSA ICYMI roundup, Oct. 18, 2026. Original sources: Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026; Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026; Florida National Guard, Army.mil, Oct. 6, 2026.
